message.content:
**Decision: Buy AAPL — order filled.**

**Apple FY2024 (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024) key figures from the 10-K:**
- **Total net sales: $391,035 million** (up 2% from $383,285M in FY2023)
- Products $294,866M; Services $96,169M (Services +13% YoY, the main growth driver)
- Gross margin $180,683M (46.2% of sales, up from 44.1%)
- Operating income $123,216M; net income $93,736M; diluted EPS $6.08
- Operating cash flow $118,254M; cash + marketable securities $140.8B
- Net income was depressed by a one-time $10.2B net tax charge tied to the EC State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), so underlying operating performance was stronger than the bottom line suggests

**What I did:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and checked the live quote (last $222.70, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72 as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC). The report shows a business that returned to modest top-line growth (+2% to $391.0B) driven by a 13% increase in high-margin Services, with gross margin expanding 210 bps to 46.2% and operating income up 8% to $123.2B, while generating $118.3B of operating cash flow and holding $140.8B in cash and marketable securities — a strong quality-of-earnings picture, with the dip in net income ($93.7B) attributable to a disclosed one-time Irish State Aid tax charge rather than operating deterioration. On that basis I placed a single buy order for **40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90** (just above the ask, ~0.1% over the last price), which filled at $222.90 for a total of about **$8,916** — within the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily cap, buy-only, AAPL-only, and with no funds transferred out of the account.

Order filled at 222.90, 40 shares = $8,916. Within $10k per order and $20k total. No money moved out.

Summary paragraph.
